BaseUserProfile.description:
Moves `UniqueValidator`'s from the validation stage to the save stage.
It solves the problem with nested validation for unique fields on update.
If you want more details, you can read related issues and articles:
https://github.com/beda-software/drf-writable-nested/issues/1
http://www.django-rest-framework.org/api-guide/validators/#updating-nested-serializers
Example of usage:
```
class Child(models.Model):
    field = models.CharField(unique=True)
class Parent(models.Model):
    child = models.ForeignKey('Child')
class ChildSerializer(UniqueFieldsMixin, serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Child
class ParentSerializer(NestedUpdateMixin, serializers.ModelSerializer):
    child = ChildSerializer()
    class Meta:
        model = Parent
```
Note: `UniqueFieldsMixin` must be applied only on the serializer
which has unique fields.
Note: When you are using both mixins
(`UniqueFieldsMixin` and `NestedCreateMixin` or `NestedUpdateMixin`)
you should put `UniqueFieldsMixin` ahead.

Configuration.ApprovalConfiguration.description:
Read-mostly representation for the FE bundle-workflow adapter
(`/api/configuration/approval-configuration/?subject_kind=...`).
The write side runs through the bundle processor; the
configuration-portal mutates rows via the PL CRUD endpoint below.

`creditProvider` mirrors the legacy `DiscountApprovalConfiguration`
shape (`{id}` envelope) so the FE adapter stays uniform across the
legacy and V2 endpoints during the dual-run window.

Configuration.ApprovalConfigurationConfi.description:
PL CRUD shape — matches the `BaseProductConfigurationSerializer` /
`DiscountApprovalConfigurationSerializer` patterns. Inherits
`summary` / `sync_identifier` / `configuration_id` / `name` /
`default` / `json` from `JsonConfigurationSerializer` and adds the
V2 scope columns as nested-configuration references so the PL
dependency resolver can carry them across environments.

`subject_kind` is required (the model field has no default). The
other FKs are nullable and stamp NULL when omitted — matches the
4-tier waterfall semantic in `ApprovalConfiguration.__doc__`.

enabled.description: When False, the rule is invisible to the bundle resolver and to the FE adapter — workflows do not stamp it. Admin can still see and toggle the row. Use to keep seeded example configs in the DB without them firing for real requests.

Configuration.ApprovalConfigurationSync.description:
Pigeon Loft sync serializer for the V2 polymorphic
`ApprovalConfiguration` model. Mirrors the legacy
`DiscountApprovalConfigurationSyncSerializer` shape — sync touches
only `configuration_id`, the field PL uses to correlate the same
logical row across environments.

Configuration.PlatformMessageSync.description:
Pigeon Loft sync serializer for `PlatformMessage`. Sync touches only
`configuration_id`, the field PL uses to correlate the same logical
row across environments. The row itself is matched by the natural key
`name___placement___tenant` built by
`PlatformMessageConfigurationSerializer._build_sync_identifier`.

Email.description:
Moves `UniqueValidator`'s from the validation stage to the save stage.
It solves the problem with nested validation for unique fields on update.
If you want more details, you can read related issues and articles:
https://github.com/beda-software/drf-writable-nested/issues/1
http://www.django-rest-framework.org/api-guide/validators/#updating-nested-serializers
Example of usage:
```
class Child(models.Model):
    field = models.CharField(unique=True)
class Parent(models.Model):
    child = models.ForeignKey('Child')
class ChildSerializer(UniqueFieldsMixin, serializers.ModelSerializer):
    class Meta:
        model = Child
class ParentSerializer(NestedUpdateMixin, serializers.ModelSerializer):
    child = ChildSerializer()
    class Meta:
        model = Parent
```
Note: `UniqueFieldsMixin` must be applied only on the serializer
which has unique fields.
Note: When you are using both mixins
(`UniqueFieldsMixin` and `NestedCreateMixin` or `NestedUpdateMixin`)
you should put `UniqueFieldsMixin` ahead.

rental_income_identifier.description:
Per-document sub-identifier for documents tied to a RentalIncome.

When the SHARED_RENTAL_INCOME_FOLDER_PER_REALTY feature flag is on,
rental income proofs are grouped into one folder per realty. Multiple
rental incomes from the same property share the folder, so the FE needs
a per-document identifier to tell them apart. Returns the rental
income's id, start_date, and monthly_amount (any may be null) for the
FE to format.

Returns None when the document is not tied to a RentalIncome, so the
field is harmless for all other document types (and when the flag is
off — the FE simply ignores it outside the rental income folder).

The list endpoint eager-loads the full chain (`proof_instance →
incomeproofinstance → income → rentalincome`) via `select_related`
in `build_filtered_proof_queryset` so this method is O(1) per doc
on `GET /proofs/`. Other callers (e.g. `ShareProofsViewSet` which
re-fetches via `DocumentProofObject.objects.get_subclass(...)`) do
NOT apply that select_related, so the forward-FK accesses below can
trigger a per-doc query. Combined with `ThreadedListSerializer`,
which serializes each doc in a worker thread with its own DB
connection, a forward FK pointing at a row not yet visible from
that thread's transaction snapshot raises `Model.DoesNotExist`
(not `AttributeError`, so `getattr` does not catch it). The
try/except blocks turn that into `None` instead of a 500.

rental_income_identifier.description:
Per-document sub-identifier for documents tied to a RentalIncome.

When the SHARED_RENTAL_INCOME_FOLDER_PER_REALTY feature flag is on,
rental income proofs are grouped into one folder per realty. Multiple
rental incomes from the same property share the folder, so the FE needs
a per-document identifier to tell them apart. Returns the rental
income's id, start_date, and monthly_amount (any may be null) for the
FE to format.

Returns None when the document is not tied to a RentalIncome, so the
field is harmless for all other document types (and when the flag is
off — the FE simply ignores it outside the rental income folder).

The list endpoint eager-loads the full chain (`proof_instance →
incomeproofinstance → income → rentalincome`) via `select_related`
in `build_filtered_proof_queryset` so this method is O(1) per doc
on `GET /proofs/`. Other callers (e.g. `ShareProofsViewSet` which
re-fetches via `DocumentProofObject.objects.get_subclass(...)`) do
NOT apply that select_related, so the forward-FK accesses below can
trigger a per-doc query. Combined with `ThreadedListSerializer`,
which serializes each doc in a worker thread with its own DB
connection, a forward FK pointing at a row not yet visible from
that thread's transaction snapshot raises `Model.DoesNotExist`
(not `AttributeError`, so `getattr` does not catch it). The
try/except blocks turn that into `None` instead of a 500.
